studios.title: Noir Photo Studio
studios.description: Blackout portrait room. Ceiling grid takes four strobes and a 12-foot seamless.
overview: Noir is a single-room portrait studio built for photographers who want the frame under total control. Blacked-out walls, a ceiling grid rated for four strobes, and a 12-foot seamless roll in white, black, and grey — switched between models without breaking your light.

The room sits on a quiet Brooklyn block with street-level load-in, a grip corner that stays organized, and a small lounge behind double doors when you need the set quiet. Best for portraits, lookbooks, and product work that lives or dies on the light.

studios.title: Blackbird Sound Stage
studios.description: Black-box stage. Roll-up doors, a 24-foot throw, and grid-locked lighting.
overview: Blackbird is a working black-box stage with roll-up doors on both ends, so trucks back in and sets go up without a shuttle run. The grid is locked and rated for real builds, and the 24-foot throw covers everything from interview setups to full performance captures.

Support spaces do the unglamorous work: a green room that seats a full crew, climate control that survives Georgia summers, and parking that can take a production van. Half-day and full-day blocks, with overnight builds by arrangement.

studios.title: Analog Music Loft
studios.description: Warm tracking room. Vintage console, live area, and a wall of guitars.
overview: A working tracking room in a converted Nashville warehouse: a serviced vintage console, a live area that takes a drum kit and a small band at once, and a wall of guitars and amps included in the rate. The control room looks straight into the live room through a single pane of glass.

Sessions run on house power that was wired for audio — no generator hum, no mystery ground loops. Wes keeps the patchbay labeled and the tea kettle on, and will engineer by the hour if your budget allows.

studios.title: The Frequency Room
studios.description: Four-seat podcast booth. Broadcast mics, full treatment, and a live engineer on request.
overview: Four seats, four broadcast mics on boom arms, and treatment on every surface — record a full panel and skip the cleanup pass. The desk takes laptops and a small switcher, so video podcasts are just as easy as audio-only.
A live mix engineer can be added to any booking, and the room is pre-wired for remote guests on a clean return. Walk in, sit down, record; the files are yours at the end of the session.

studios.title: Atelier Nord
studios.description: Gallery-style art workshop. Track lighting, a wet station, and sixteen easels.
overview: A working atelier with sixteen adjustable easels, a wet station that survives a full class day, and track lighting calibrated to read color true — hang a show, teach a workshop, or take the room for a private studio day.
North-facing windows give even morning light, and lockable storage means materials stay between sessions. The room cleans down fast, and the washout station is plumbed for clay as well as paint.

studios.title: Ember Vocal Suite
studios.description: Isolated vocal booth. Tube condenser, zero-latency cue mix, and a dimmer for mood.
overview: One room, one job: vocals. Ember is an isolated booth around a tube condenser, with a zero-latency cue mix and a dimmer that lets you set the mood for a long session. The sound floor is low enough for whisper takes.
The adjoining control nook handles comping while the singer stays warm in the booth. Book by the hour for overdubs or grab an evening block for a full vocal production day.

studios.title: Daybreak Loft Studio
studios.description: North-facing loft. Ten-foot windows flood the cove from sunrise to dusk.
overview: A daylight loft built around ten-foot windows that flood the cove from sunrise to dusk — no flags, no bounce boards, just honest north light for most of the working day. The white cove sweeps wide enough for movement and small vehicle props.
Downstairs load-in, a styling corner with two makeup stations, and an espresso bar that keeps crews on site. Popular for brand films, lookbooks, and anything that wants soft, forgiving daylight.

studios.title: The Print Lab
studios.description: Daylight print lab. Copy table, garment rack, and a seamless wall for styling.
overview: A daylight prep-and-shoot room for the work that happens around a shoot: a copy table under even north light, garment racks for styling, and a seamless wall for the frames that need to happen between fittings.

Rae's second Brooklyn space, run with the same standards as Noir — organized, quiet, and priced for the small crew that doesn't need a stage. Lockable storage keeps client samples safe between bookings.

studios.title: The Foundry Stage
studios.description: Converted foundry bay. Steel trusses span forty feet overhead.
overview: A converted foundry bay with forty feet of clear span under steel trusses that took our last three rigging plans without an exception. Column-free floor, 30kW of power, and a loading dock a box truck can back straight into.
The bones are industrial and honest: concrete floor, high bay doors, and enough height to build tall. Step-free throughout, with a green room and catering corner at the back for long shoot days.

studios.title: Signal Podcast Suite
studios.description: Glass-walled podcast suite. River views beyond the faders.
overview: A glass-walled suite above the river with a broadcast-ready signal chain: five mic positions, a monitor controller, and routing that flatters every voice we've run through it. Video podcasts look as good as they sound — river light does the background work.
Ben hosts most mornings himself and will walk first-timers through the routing in ten minutes. Monthly blocks are common for weekly shows; mornings book out fastest.

studios.title: Riverside Music Suite
studios.description: Live room over the river. Yamaha grand, drum riser, and variable acoustics.
overview: A live room on the water with a Yamaha grand that stays tuned, a permanent drum riser, and variable acoustic panels that genuinely change the decay of the space. Track a ballad in the morning and a full band at night without moving a chair.
June engineered on enough records to know what a session needs before it asks — the patchbay is labeled, the headphone mixes are sane, and the river view does something quiet to a long day.

studios.title: Clay & Kiln Studio
studios.description: Ceramics workshop. Six wheels, two kilns, and a dedicated washout station.
overview: A ceramics workshop that runs like a classroom: six wheels, two kilns on a published firing schedule, and a washout station plumbed for clay so the space is clean at the end of every session. Glaze-testing notes live on the wall, courtesy of Ivy.
Book the room for a class, a residency block, or a firing weekend. Materials and firings are billed separately by arrangement, and lockable storage keeps work-in-progress between visits.

studios.title: The Maker Lounge
studios.description: Bright maker lounge. Soft seating, sample tables, and space to pin up work.
overview: A bright, calm lounge for the collaborative parts of creative work: sample tables big enough to unroll a collection, pin-up walls for a full day of reviews, and soft seating that makes a residency feel like a residency.
Step-free throughout, with an espresso bar and lockable storage for materials. Ivy's second space suits workshops, portfolio reviews, and small teams who need a room that isn't an office.

reviews.comment: The blackout is total — gels read exactly as metered and the grid held four strobes without a flicker.
Booked for a full day and never once fought the space. Rae had the seamless changed between models.
Beautiful light and quiet street access. Street parking is tight, but the studio itself is flawless.
Those windows earn their keep. We chased the light from nine until two and never moved a fixture.
The cove takes a full cyclorama sweep and the espresso bar kept a crew of nine caffeinated.
Genuinely lovely room. Afternoons get warm by the glass, so book the climate control early.
Copy table, garment racks, and a styling corner — it's the prep space every other shoot was missing.
North light stayed even all afternoon. Printed proofs on the table by the end of the booking.
Compact but brilliantly organized. The prop library saved us a rental fee on set dressing.
Roll-up doors on both ends made the load-in a breeze. The lighting grid is properly rigged for a real build.
24 feet of throw and a green room that actually fits the talent. We'll be back for the next campaign.
Floor is sprung enough for our dancers. Bring earplugs for the generator hum next door.
Forty feet of clear span and a loading dock a truck can back right into. Rare at this price.
Industrial bones, serious power. The trusses took our rigging plan without a single exception.
We built a 60-foot runway and the crew still had room to work around it. Priya is a great host.
The console is serviced and the live room is gorgeous. We tracked drums and vocals without swapping rooms.
Wesley knows every cable in the place and it shows. Patched in and tracking within twenty minutes.
Warm room, characterful gear. The guitar wall is dangerous for the credit card.
The grand is tuned and voiced properly, and the river view does something for the mood of a session.
Variable acoustics panels genuinely work. Quiet enough for vocals loud enough for a band.
Booked the evening block twice now. The drum riser stays set, which saved us an hour each time.
Zero-latency cue mix and a booth you can actually trust. Did twelve takes without touching an edit.
Tube condenser is the real thing. The dimmer is a small touch that makes long sessions kinder.
Consistent sound floor, thoughtful acoustics. Tomas had the patchbay diagram printed for me.
Four seats, broadcast mics, no editing afterwards. The live engineer option is worth every dollar.
Treatment on every surface means the room simply disappears in the mix. Alicia is a gracious host.
Compact for four, which is exactly the promise. Booked three blocks back to back with no issues.
Glass walls, river light, and a signal chain that flatters every voice we've put through it.
Ben walked us through the routing in ten minutes and left us to it. Client thrilled with the audio.
Great room for a four-mic panel. Mornings book out fast — grab the slot early.
Sixteen easels, a wet station that survives a full day, and track lighting that reads color true.
North light in the morning is exactly right for drawing. Lockable storage kept our materials safe.
It feels like a real working atelier, not a rented room. Marta left the good brushes out for us.
Six wheels, two kilns firing on schedule, and a washout station that doesn't quit. Ideal classroom.
Booked both kilns for a firing weekend. Ivy's glaze notes taped to the wall saved me hours.
Wonderful, unpretentious workspace. Bring an apron — the clay sink means you'll actually use it.
Soft seating, big sample tables, and wall space to pin an entire collection. Our team moved in happily.
Bright and calm all day. The espresso bar earned more compliments than the work did.
Step-free access mattered for one of our guests, and the whole space just feels considered.
